llm.summary: This skill matches its Amazon order-management purpose, but it stores full order responses locally by default and can change shipment or verification state without a built-in confirmation step.

dimensions.detail: The documented capabilities, scripts, and API paths all align with Amazon SP-API order lookup, buyer/address retrieval, shipment updates, regulated-order checks, and shipment confirmation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill handles sensitive buyer/address/order data and state-changing POST/PATCH actions; the docs disclose the APIs but do not provide clear runtime consent, redaction, dry-run, or role-scoping controls for the highest-impact operations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No installer, obfuscation, package download, or hidden setup behavior was found; scripts are plain Python files and a dependency check only looks for the companion auth skill.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network access to the LinkFox gateway and Amazon proxy is expected, but always writing full API responses to local session files is broader than necessary for routine order lookup and may persist customer PII.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md says full responses are always saved under a linkfox session directory, and the helper also falls back to home or temp directories despite the documentation saying /tmp is forbidden; there is no retention, encryption, or opt-in control.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with local files containing full Amazon order, buyer, address, regulated-order, and shipment data. Use it in a controlled workspace, delete saved linkfox session data when no longer needed, avoid --inline for sensitive responses, and require explicit human review before running shipment confirmation, shipment-status update, or verification-status update scripts.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Environment variables, network calls, shell execution of the dependency checker, and local writes are understandable for this integration, but the skill lacks a clear permissions and control model for sensitive order data.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed: emit_result writes complete result JSON to disk for every operation, which can include buyer, address, regulated-order, or shipment data.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed in part: the shared helper creates session metadata and indexes saved data files; useful for workflow continuity, but excessive for sensitive order responses without retention or minimization controls.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed: SKILL.md discloses default full-response persistence, but there is no opt-in, redaction, or warning at the point where buyer/address data may be saved or printed.
[SQP-2] expected: The docs correctly describe token retrieval and proxy use, and mention RDT/data-protection requirements, but token and PII handling guidance is thin for this data class.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed: the code saves full responses first and only reports the saved path afterward.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed: confirm_shipment.py performs a live POST after required parameters are supplied, with no built-in confirmation flag or dry-run mode.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed: get_order_address.py fetches and emits shipping address data without masking or an explicit high-sensitivity gate.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed: get_order_buyer_info.py fetches and emits buyer information without masking or an explicit high-sensitivity gate.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed: get_order_items_buyer_info.py fetches and emits item-level buyer information without masking or an explicit high-sensitivity gate.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Confirmed: default persistent storage of complete order responses creates local copies outside Amazon/LinkFox access controls.
